2610.13840.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
2610.13840.paper_summary: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. We argue that artificial intelligence, including generative models, can change this to the benefit of the medium itself. We propose PAGE, a framework that makes artificial intelligence an instrument for comics research. It parses every scan into panels, text and a bibliographic record; annotates each page with a vision-language model that follows a written codebook, as a human coder would; grounds samples of these readings in human annotation; and explains change across an archive, with estimates controlled for publisher and genre. We demonstrate the framework on 3,929 American comic books (1938--1956) and 87 volumes of Japanese manga, in three studies, each resting on a different capability. The first pairs text search with visual reading to recover how a mass medium portrayed political power. The second measures the page's visual form across an industry and recovers the hand of individual artists. The third follows who speaks across two comics traditions, checked against human annotation. Beyond research, the same instruments can make archives searchable by what is drawn, open comics to blind and low-vision readers, and help preserve fragile collections and credit uncredited artists. We outline a research agenda in which artificial intelligence strengthens the study, preservation and reach of the medium.
2610.13840.paper_summary_zh: 漫畫是二十世紀偉大的視覺記錄之一：數十萬頁中，大眾讀者看到了他們的領袖、戰爭和英雄。這一記錄的大部分從未作為整體進行過研究；漫畫學術研究通常是一本一本地進行。我們認為，人工智慧，包括生成模型，可以改變這一現狀，從而使媒介本身受益。我們提出了PAGE，一個將人工智慧作為漫畫研究工具的框架。它將每個掃描解析為面板、文本和書目記錄；用遵循書面代碼本的視覺-語言模型為每頁進行註釋，正如人類編碼者所做的那樣；將這些讀取樣本與人類註釋相結合；並解釋整個檔案中的變化，並對出版商和類型進行控制估算。我們在3929本美國漫畫（1938-1956年）和87卷日本漫畫上展示了該框架，進行了三項研究，每項研究基於不同的能力。第一項將文本搜索與視覺閱讀相結合，以恢復大眾媒介如何描繪政治權力。第二項測量整個行業的頁面視覺形式，並恢復個別藝術家的風格。第三項則追蹤在兩個漫畫傳統中誰在發言，並與人類註釋進行核對。除了研究，這些工具還可以使檔案根據所繪製的內容可搜索，讓盲人和視力低下的讀者接觸漫畫，並幫助保存脆弱的收藏，給未獲得認可的藝術家以信用。我們概述了一個研究議程，其中人工智慧加強了對這一媒介的研究、保存和影響力。
